name: מערכת שתי משוואות לינאריות – מציאת x ו-y (באנגלית)
questiontext:
Given

\[ \begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle {{CT:0}}&\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:1}}\mbox{,}\\ {{CT:2}}&\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:3}}\mbox{,} \end{array} \]

then find \(x\) and \(y\):

\(x=\) [[input:ans1]]
[[validation:ans1]]
\(y=\) [[input:ans2]]
[[validation:ans2]]
generalfeedback:
Outline: Eliminate \(y\): multiply the equations so that the \(y\)-terms have the same coefficient, subtract to find \(x\), then substitute back to find \(y\).
Step 1 — Making the \(y\)-coefficients equal
We are given

\[ \begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle {{CT:0}}&\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:1}}\mbox{,}\\ {{CT:2}}&\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:3}}\mbox{.} \end{array} \]

Multiplying the first equation by {{CT:4}} and the second equation by {{CT:5}} we obtain

\[ \begin{array}{rcl}\displaystyle {{CT:6}}&\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:7}}\mbox{,}\\ {{CT:8}}&\displaystyle =&\displaystyle {{CT:9}}\mbox{.} \end{array} \]

Now \(y\) has the same coefficient, \({{CT:10}}\), in both equations.
Step 2 — Subtracting to find \(x\)
Subtracting the latter equation from the former one, the \(y\)-terms cancel. The coefficient of \({{CT:11}}\) becomes \({{CT:12}}-\left({{CT:13}}\right)={{CT:14}}\), and the right-hand side becomes \({{CT:7}}-\left({{CT:9}}\right)={{CT:15}}\):

\[ {{CT:16}}={{CT:15}} \]

Dividing by \({{CT:14}}\):

\[ x=\frac{{{CT:15}}}{{{CT:14}}}={{CT:17}} \]

Step 3 — Substituting back to find \(y\)
Substituting \(x={{CT:17}}\) in the former equation \({{CT:6}}={{CT:7}}\):

\[ {{CT:18}}={{CT:7}}-\left({{CT:12}}\right)\times\left({{CT:17}}\right)={{CT:19}} \]

and dividing by \({{CT:10}}\):

\[ y=\frac{{{CT:19}}}{{{CT:10}}}={{CT:20}} \]

Step 4 — Check
Substituting into the original equations:

\[ {{CT:21}}\cdot\left({{CT:17}}\right)+\left({{CT:22}}\right)\cdot\left({{CT:20}}\right)={{CT:1}} \]

\[ {{CT:23}}\cdot\left({{CT:17}}\right)+\left({{CT:24}}\right)\cdot\left({{CT:20}}\right)={{CT:3}} \]

Both equations balance, so

\[ x={{CT:17}},\qquad y={{CT:20}} \]

on_true.feedback: You can check your answer by substituting for \(x\) and \(y\) and confirming that the equations balance.

on_false.feedback:
Substituting \(x={@ans1@}\) and \(y={@ans2@}\)

\[ {{CT:0}}={@ansg1@} \]

\[ {{CT:2}}={@ansg2@} \]

but substituting in the unique correct values for \(x\) and \(y\) the above equations should evaluate to {{CT:25}} and {{CT:26}} respectively.

on_true.feedback: When you multiply an equation by a constant, remember to multiply both sides, the right hand-side as well as the left hand-side.
It may be that you added the two equations when you should have subtracted one from the other.
